turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of your class, and nobody called me first. Start with why.
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.
A machine's guess is not a finding, Hale. Even the company that sells that checker says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have, or is that it?
I don't need more proof than that.
"Don't need" is not an answer. Who decided to enter the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before they did?
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
Are you calling my son a liar? He doesn't lie. Put that comparison in an email if you want to keep it, and then tell me who decided.
Then we're going to the principal, because you've entered a mark on a checker's score and no meeting first. I'm writing that down.
